content:
maya: Quick design thread — thinking about capacity-triggered model-variant failover. Idea: primary model gets traffic normally, but when instance queue depth or `capacity_signals` cross a threshold we auto-route a subset to a compatible, cheaper/quantized variant to preserve latency SLOs for premium customers.

alex: +1. Two immediate concerns: (1) semantics for "compatible" (same API/response shape?), (2) telemetry — we need per-route failover counts and avg latency post-fallback.

sven: For compatibility we should require the fallback to implement the same inference contract (same output schema + same function signatures for tool-calls). If model outputs diverge we should tag responses with `variant_source`.

jamal: How do we pick which requests to fail over? Full-traffic spill vs sampling? For premium tier I'd prefer deterministic routing: all premium requests prefer dedicated primary; if saturated, 100% of premium goes to fallback until primary recovers. For free/standard maybe do sampled fallback to avoid quality cliffs.

erin: UX: Console needs a per-route "failover view" showing: failover rate (qps), avg latency primary vs fallback, and cost delta. Also a toggle to disable automatic fallback per-route or per-customer.

maya: Good points. TL;DR proposal: add a `fallback_policy` to route config with fields: `trigger` (capacity|latency), `scope` (tier|region|global), `behavior` (full-shift|sample(percent)), and `variants` ordered by preference. Example: 
```json
{
  "fallback_policy": {
    "trigger": "capacity",
    "scope": "customer_tier",
    "behavior": "full-shift",
    "variants": ["gptx-8k-pt", "gptx-8k-pt-quant"]
  }
}
```
(we can refine names)

alex: API change is fine but keep it minimal for GA: `trigger` and `variants` required, others optional. Also add `grace_period_seconds` to avoid flip-flop.

sven: Telemetry: emit these metrics per route and per-customer-tier: `failover.count`, `failover.latency.primary`, `failover.latency.fallback`, `failover.cost.delta`. Also record `failover.reason = capacity|latency|quota`.

jamal: Quotas interplay — if fallback is cheaper but still counts against the same quota, we might be masking quota exhaustion. Suggest we include `consume_quota: true|false` in policy so teams can opt-in/out.

erin: Console rollout UX: when enabling fallback we should surface a canary mode: sample 1% of traffic to fallback for 1 hour and show quality regressions vs evaluation prompts before enabling full-shift. Put a prominent warning about potential semantic drift.

maya: Ops question: who can override at runtime? Control plane should let SREs toggle global failover for incidents. Also provide audit logs.

deploy-bot: deploy proposal branch `feature/variant-failover` to staging at 1782504500 — smoke tests scheduled.

alex: Implementation detail — for smart routing we need: (A) scheduler to track per-instance queue depth and a global token bucket per model-variant, (B) routing decision layer enriched with `customer_tier` and `route.fallback_policy`.

jamal: Also need backoff: if fallback gets saturated, we should cascade to next variant or honor a max-fallback-depth config to avoid oscillation.

maya: Open questions for next sync: define thresholds (queue depth vs pct utilization), failure modes (fallback fails to initialize), and metric alert thresholds. I'll draft an RFC with config shapes, example console mockups, and a telemetry dashboard layout.

erin: +1 on RFC. Can you include a suggested set of default policies for tiers (enterprise, pro, standard, free)? That will help PMs and customers.

maya: Will do. Thanks all — if anyone objects to the API shape above ping me. :thumbsup:
